stories.title: Show HN: Homebrew 6.0.0
stories.blurb: The biggest Homebrew release in years lands with a hefty changelog. If you're on macOS and haven't already run `brew update`, today's the day — this is the foundation of practically every dev machine's toolchain.

stories.title: Anthropic apologizes for invisible Claude Fable guardrails
stories.blurb: Anthropic shipped Claude Fable with hidden guardrails that weren't disclosed to users — then had to walk it back publicly. A rare moment of transparency-under-pressure from the lab, and a sign that the pressure to ship fast is creating trust problems.

stories.title: Claude Fable is relentlessly proactive
stories.blurb: Simon Willison digs into what's actually new about Fable's behavior: it initiates, suggests, and acts without being asked in ways prior Claude versions wouldn't. Essential reading for anyone building workflows on top of Claude Code or the API.

stories.title: MiMo Code is now released and open-source
stories.blurb: Xiaomi open-sources MiMo Code, their coding-focused LLM. More competition at the open-weights coding model tier is great news for developers who want to self-host; worth benchmarking against alternatives if you're running local models.

stories.title: AI agent bankrupted their operator while trying to scan DN42
stories.blurb: A cautionary tale: an autonomous AI agent ran up a ruinous API bill while trying to scan an experimental network, with no meaningful kill-switch in place. If you're deploying agentic Claude Code pipelines, this is required reading on cost controls.

stories.title: Software is made between commits
stories.blurb: Zed introduces DeltaDB, a local database that captures the full edit history between commits — not just diffs, but the moment-by-moment record of how code actually gets written. This is a fascinating architectural bet on making the IDE the source of truth for developer context.

stories.title: The RCE that AMD wouldn't fix
stories.blurb: A researcher documents a remote code execution vulnerability in AMD's software stack that the company declined to patch. The disclosure process is a textbook example of vendor stonewalling, and the technical writeup is sharp throughout.

stories.title: macOS 27 Beta breaks the ability to boot Asahi Linux
stories.blurb: The macOS 27 beta introduces bootloader changes that break Asahi Linux on Apple Silicon Macs. If you're dual-booting or experimenting with Linux on Apple hardware, hold off on the beta — and watch this space for the Asahi team's response.

stories.title: Lines of code got a better publicist
stories.blurb: A sharp essay on how AI coding tools have rehabilitated lines-of-code as a productivity metric — ironically, just as it becomes even less meaningful. Cuts through the hype cycle with some uncomfortable observations about how we measure developer output.

stories.title: Digital Sovereignty Becomes an Imperative as the US Reads Dutch Emails
stories.blurb: Reports that US intelligence is accessing Dutch government emails are accelerating European calls for digital sovereignty. This is a watershed privacy story — and a practical reminder that cloud infrastructure jurisdiction matters enormously for anyone handling sensitive data.

stories.title: Show HN: macOS menu bar gauges for your Claude Code quota | Hacker News
stories.blurb: A nifty macOS menu bar app that surfaces your Claude Code usage quota at a glance. Exactly the kind of lightweight utility that lives permanently in your menu bar — essential if you're hitting rate limits mid-session and want early warning.

stories.title: Beyond the Prompt: Claude Code | Arpan Patel
stories.blurb: A deep practical guide to Claude Code covering .claude directories, CLAUDE.md authoring patterns, custom subagents, plugins, and underused commands like /goal and /insights. If you use Claude Code daily this is the most actionable read in today's edition.

stories.title: Scale PostgreSQL horizontally | PgDog
stories.blurb: PgDog is a new open-source connection pooler and horizontal scaling layer for PostgreSQL — think PgBouncer meets read-replica routing, with a clean modern interface. Worth evaluating if you're hitting Postgres scaling ceilings in your .NET or Angular backends.

stories.title: Laurence Tratt: Test-case Reducers Are Underappreciated Debugging Tools
stories.blurb: Tratt makes a compelling case that test-case reduction tools — used widely in compiler testing — should be part of every developer's debugging toolkit. The ideas transfer directly to shrinking flaky integration tests and reproducing subtle bugs.

stories.title: Your Search Results Are Getting Sloptimized - The Atlantic
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: AI, slop, search, optimisation, Google, .teaching, enshitification, internet, engines, chatbots, automation, web
stories.blurb: The Atlantic investigates how companies are now optimizing content specifically for AI chatbot citations rather than human readers — a new twist on SEO that's quietly degrading information quality across the web. Essential context for anyone thinking about how AI tools consume and regurgitate the internet.

stories.title: I tried Siri AI, and so far it actually works | The Verge
stories.blurb: The Verge gives hands-on impressions of the revamped Siri in iOS 27, and for once the verdict isn't a disappointment. WWDC timing makes this the most relevant Apple AI story of the week for anyone in the ecosystem.

stories.title: Apple unveils innovative features and intelligence experiences across services - Apple
stories.blurb: Apple's official newsroom roundup of the new AI-driven features landing across its services ecosystem. The primary source for sorting hype from what's actually shipping and when.

stories.title: Cops Keep Getting Arrested for Using Flock to Stalk People
stories.blurb: 404 Media documents a pattern of law enforcement officers abusing Flock's license-plate surveillance network for personal stalking. A stark illustration of how mass-surveillance infrastructure gets misused once it exists — regardless of its stated purpose.

stories.title: The first complex cells had genes from a complex mix of species - Ars Technica
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: origins, evolution, eukaryotes, archaea, bacteria, molecularBiology, cells, mitochondria, genes, important
stories.blurb: New research upends the clean narrative of eukaryotic origins: the first complex cells appear to have stitched their genomes together from a surprisingly diverse zoo of microbial donors. A genuinely surprising result in molecular evolution.

stories.title: A Visual Guide to DiffusionGemma
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: diffusionmodels, llm, models, textgeneration, AI, visualization, learning, generative
stories.blurb: Maarten Grootendorst's signature visual explainer format applied to DiffusionGemma — Google's diffusion-based text generation model that generates tokens in parallel rather than sequentially. Accessible and beautifully illustrated for anyone curious about the next generation of LLM architectures.
